title: Mbakhal with Peanut Flour
author: Amina Savoura
desc: The same buried-nététou-ball rice, with 250 g of raw peanut flour sprinkled over before the lid goes on.
longDesc: Afrik’s peanut mbakhal is the fisherman’s version with one addition: long-grain rice, and 250 g of raw peanut flour sprinkled over the rice before covering. The skeleton is unchanged — tiof head and dried fish boiled in salted water, nététou pounded with chile and onion into the broth, rice cooked in the sauce with two fingers of liquid above it, a second nététou ball buried in the centre and removed after 20 minutes, the finished plate topped with cooked nététou and drizzled with butter or palm oil.
ingredients: 1 tiof head, or 600 g fresh fish
steps: Boil the tiof head and dried fish in salted water. Pound 25 g of nététou with a chile and the onion and stir the paste in.
Remove the fish and keep warm. Cook the rice in the sauce, leaving two fingers of liquid above the rice at the start; add hot water if needed.
Pound the remaining nététou with the second chile and salt and form a ball. Bury it in a well in the rice.
Sprinkle the raw peanut flour over everything, cover and continue cooking.
Serve the fish with the rice, top with the cooked nététou mixture and drizzle with indigenous butter or palm oil.
chefTips: The method is SINGLE-PASS — treat the quantities as a guide until checked against the printed page.
The peanut flour goes in raw and is cooked only by the covered steam; the page prints no cue for when it is done.
Two fingers of liquid above the rice at the start is the printed cue for the water.
Use long-grain rice as printed; the other mbakhal says only ‘riz’.
commonMistakes: Adding the flour into the liquid so it lumps instead of sprinkling over.
Forgetting to remove the nététou ball.
reheating: Steam gently with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Peanut flour supplies protein and healthy fats.
culturalNote: The page’s total time is 2 hours, prep and cooking together. Mbakhal is a Wolof dish; a Saloum version, with dried shrimp, yet and guedj, is at SEN039.
sources: Title as printed: ‘MBakahl aux arachides’ — note the capitalisation and the spelling ‘MBakahl’, which differs from ‘Mbakhal’ on the same site. Byline: ‘Amina Savoura’. Publication: Afrik. Published ‘16 septembre 2012 à 10h46’, updated ‘13 avril 2026 à 18h41’. Yield: none printed (6 is an estimate). Total time as printed: 2 hours.

SINGLE-PASS. The fetch tool refused verbatim transcription on the one attempt and returned a paraphrase. Every figure is single-pass, and the wording is the fetcher’s, except the one quoted line: ‘Pilez 25 grs de nététou avec un piment et l’oignon.’

Ingredients, SINGLE-PASS: 250 g raw peanut powder; 1 kg long-grain rice; 125 g nététou; 1 large onion; 2 chiles; 1 head of tiof or 600 g fresh fish; 1 piece of dried fish; 100 g clarified indigenous butter; lemons (no quantity).

DIFFERENCE from SEN037, as printed: 250 g of raw peanut powder is sprinkled over the dish before the covered cooking, and the rice is specified long-grain. NO CUE, TIME ONLY for the peanut flour: the 20 minutes attaches to the nététou ball, not to the flour.
Guedj, yeet and kecc do not appear on this page. A further lead, ‘From the Kitchen: Mbahal’ by Jessica Fryman, was not fetched.
